regime_label: Guarani per US dollar, administered regime, 1945-1969
evidence: exchange_rates 'USD Fin Mes', annual end-of-period quotations 1945-1969 (3.12 to 147.50), against 'USD Prom' monthly averages from 1989 (1004.80 to 7983.86). The 1951-52 devaluation is visible as a step from 3.12 to 31.50.
proposal_evidence: exchange_rates 'USD Fin Mes' publishes annual end-of-period quotations from 1945 to 1969 running 3.12 to 147.50, while 'USD Prom' publishes monthly averages from 1989 running 1004.80 to 7983.86. The unit is correct in both -- the guarani was introduced in 1943 near 3 per dollar and the 1951-52 devaluation is visible as a step from 3.12 to 31.50 -- so this is not a unit defect. It is two different quotation regimes with a twenty-year hole between them.
source_cell: exchange_rates/USD Fin Mes and exchange_rates/USD Prom
proposed_by: claude-opus-5, drafted from published worksheet titles and column labels
open_questions: The audit's ER-01.4 asks whether the early range is a redenomination, an inverse quotation, a different concept or a parsing issue. The evidence here says a different regime, but the 1970-1988 gap is unexplained and the BCP's own methodological note has not been consulted. An unqualified splice of the two series is prohibited either way.

regime_label: Consumer price index, spliced series, base December 2017 = 100
evidence: CUADRO 15 title: 'Indice de precios al consumidor - Area Metropolitana de Asuncion. ... Base Diciembre 2017 = 100. Serie Empalmada'.
proposal_evidence: CUADRO 15's own title reads 'Indice de precios al consumidor - Area Metropolitana de Asuncion. Inflacion total, inflacion subyacente e inflacion subyacente (X1). Base Diciembre 2017 = 100. Serie Empalmada'. 'Serie Empalmada' is the publisher stating that the series is spliced, so the pre-2017 history is not on the same basket as the post-2017 history.
proposed_by: claude-opus-5, drafted from published worksheet titles and column labels
open_questions: The publisher says the series is spliced but not where the joins are or which earlier bases were used. The rebase dates are needed before a level comparison across them is defensible.
